entry.title: Closing Thoughts: Beyond the Grade
entry.content:
As Semester 2 draws to a close, my results are still pending. Honestly, I do not know what the numbers will say. There are assignments I wish I had started earlier, nights I wish had gone differently, and moments I would approach with more preparation if I could go back.

But I also know this: no grade will fully capture what this semester actually was.

It was the semester I stepped into leadership for the first time. The semester I hosted a ceremony in front of a full audience and held my ground. The semester I spent a sleepless night alone with a project and came out the other side. The semester I learned what I was made of — not from a textbook, but from experience.

Whatever the grades say, Semester 2 gave me something more lasting: the knowledge that I can handle pressure, carry responsibility, and keep going when it gets hard.

On to Semester 3 — with more to prove, and more to give.

entry.title: A Year with Dr. Bilal: Learning Through Trust and Structure

link.title: A Year with Dr. Bilal: Learning Through Trust and Structure

entry.content:
My entire first year was spent under the supervision of Dr. Bilal, and looking back, I feel genuinely grateful for that experience.

Sir’s approach to teaching and supervision was one that gave students space. He trusted us to take ownership of our work, to manage our time, and to figure things out on our own. That kind of autonomy is rare, and for someone who learns best by doing, it was deeply valuable. It pushed me to be more self-directed, more proactive, and more honest with myself about where I was and where I needed to be.

At the same time, Sir was not hands-off to the point of being absent. When he sensed that students were drifting or losing focus, he stepped in — calmly but firmly — and set deadlines that brought everyone back on track. It was a balance that worked well. The freedom to grow, and the structure to keep from getting lost.

All in all, the year spent under his guidance was one I look back on with appreciation. He created an environment where both learning and accountability could coexist, and that shaped how I approach my work even now.

entry.title: DBMS Exhibition: One Night, One Project, One Turning Point

link.title: DBMS Exhibition: One Night, One Project, One Turning Point

entry.content:
Of all the moments this semester, the night before the Database Management Systems (DBMS) Exhibition is the one I will remember most clearly.

I had one night. That was all the time I had left. And every part of the project — the database design, the model training, the final polish — still needed to be done. I sat down and started working, determined to see it through. Hour after hour passed. The work was slow, and the night felt endless.

Somewhere in those early morning hours, the exhaustion and the pressure reached a point I could not hold back anymore. I broke down and cried. It was not a moment of weakness — it was simply a moment of being human. The weight of the semester, the sleepless nights, the pressure of performance — it all surfaced at once.

But I did not stop. I wiped my tears, took a breath, and went back to work. By the time the sun came up, the database was fully designed and the project was ready for submission.

That night changed something in me. It taught me, in the most personal way possible, that resilience is not about never struggling. It is about choosing to continue — even when you are running on nothing but will. I walked into that exhibition not just with a project, but with a story of what it took to get there.

👨‍🏫 Supervised by Dr. Bilal Ahmad

This project — Tobacco Use Prediction System (Machine Learning Based Regression Model) — was presented by Nahida Wishad Ali Khan and Summiya Tabassum Ali, under the supervision of Dr. Bilal Ahmad.

entry.title: Three Exhibitions in One Week
entry.content:
The final weeks of the semester were, without question, the most demanding stretch I have faced so far in university. Within a single week, there were three exhibitions — all requiring preparation, presentation, and performance at the same time.

It was exhausting in a way that is difficult to fully describe. Sleep was short. The days blurred together. Every hour felt like it needed to be accounted for. But there is something remarkable about what pressure like that reveals about a person — and about a team. We pushed through, day and night, supporting each other and keeping ourselves going. By the end of that week, I was tired in every sense of the word, but I was also proud. Not just of what was submitted, but of the fact that we did not fold when it got hard.

entry.title: DLD Project: Building the Fastest Finger Game

link.title: DLD Project: Building the Fastest Finger Game

entry.content:
In Digital Logic Design, my group and I took on a project that was as challenging as it was exciting — a Fastest Finger Game, a circuit-based system designed to detect and display which player pressed their button first.

The concept was straightforward enough, but the execution was anything but. We ran into significant issues during the circuit implementation phase. Connections that should have worked did not, outputs were inconsistent, and there were moments where the whole thing felt too far from working to fix in time. But we did not give up. We sat with the problem, tested, revised, and pushed through — and eventually, we got it working.

The DLD Exhibition was the first of the semester, and presenting a project that we had genuinely struggled with made the moment of completion feel all the more satisfying. It was a reminder that the projects worth being proud of are rarely the ones that came easily.

entry.title: Leadership in Female Core: Two Roles, One Semester

link.title: Leadership in Female Core: Two Roles, One Semester

entry.content:
This semester, I also took on two distinct roles within the Female Core, each bringing its own set of challenges and lessons.

Head of Tug of War — Female Core

This was my first time managing an event as a Head. The role required coordinating with both students and faculty, handling logistics, ensuring participation, and making decisions on the spot. I had never held this kind of responsibility before, and going into it, I was not entirely sure how it would go. But it did go well. I learned how to communicate clearly under pressure, how to keep things organized when multiple things demand attention at once, and most importantly, how to lead with calm and confidence rather than anxiety. It was a small event in scale but a big step for me personally.

Director of Photography — Female Core

Alongside my Head role, I also served as Director of Photography. This position gave me the opportunity to document events visually, work creatively, and collaborate with the team in a different capacity. It was a role that required both an eye for detail and the ability to be present at every key moment — something that sharpened my sense of attentiveness and timing throughout the semester.

Together, these two roles gave me a much broader experience of what leadership and teamwork look like in practice — beyond the classroom and beyond the screen.

entry.title: Co-Hosting the IEEE Handover & Farewell Ceremony

link.title: Co-Hosting the IEEE Handover & Farewell Ceremony

entry.content:
Among all the experiences this semester brought, co-hosting the IEEE Handover & Farewell Ceremony stands out as one of the most significant. I had the honor of hosting the event alongside Asad Bhai, and together we took the stage for an occasion that carried real weight — both emotionally and professionally.

This was not a small gathering or an informal get-together. It was a proper ceremony, attended by faculty, outgoing leaders, incoming committee members, and students. Standing at that podium, managing the flow of the event, and doing it well — that felt like a turning point. It pushed me beyond my comfort zone and showed me that I was capable of holding my own on a platform that truly mattered. The experience of hosting alongside someone as experienced as Asad Bhai also taught me a great deal about stage presence, audience engagement, and the art of keeping an event moving smoothly.

entry.title: From Member to Webmaster: My Society Journey

link.title: From Member to Webmaster: My Society Journey

entry.content:
When I first joined university, I stepped into the world of student societies as a general member — curious, observant, and eager to find my place. I attended events, supported tasks wherever I could, and slowly began to understand how these organizations functioned behind the scenes. It was a quieter role, but an important one. It gave me the foundation I needed.

By the second semester, that foundation paid off. I was selected as the Webmaster of IEEE CIS (Computational Intelligence Society) — a role that came with real responsibility and real visibility. It was not just a title. It meant representing the society, managing its digital presence, and being part of a team that was working toward something meaningful. When I found out, late at night, I remember feeling genuinely overwhelmed with happiness. It was one of those moments that reminded me why showing up — even when it feels small — always matters.

entry.title: Friendships, Final Exams, and Beautiful Memories

link.title: Friendships, Final Exams, and Beautiful Memories

entry.content:
When the semester began, none of us knew each other. Over time, we became friends through lectures, laboratory sessions, assignments, and group discussions. We supported one another during exams, shared knowledge, and spent enjoyable moments together inside and outside the classroom. As the semester came to an end, we appeared in our final examinations. After completing the last paper, our entire class celebrated together with great happiness. We spent quality time, laughed together, and captured many group photographs to preserve those unforgettable memories. Looking back, my first semester was not only about studying but also about building friendships, gaining confidence, overcoming challenges, and creating memories that I will always cherish throughout my university life.

Conclusion

My first semester was the foundation of my university journey. It taught me much more than academic subjects — it taught me independence, teamwork, confidence, communication, and responsibility. From my first day in the hostel to presenting my first machine learning project and celebrating the completion of final exams, every experience contributed to my personal and professional growth. These moments will always remain a special part of my life and continue to inspire me as I move forward in my academic journey.

entry.title: Hostel Life and Personal Development
entry.content: Living in the hostel was a completely new experience for me. Staying away from home taught me how to become independent and responsible. I learned to manage my daily routine, complete assignments on time, and balance my academic and personal life. Hostel life also gave me the opportunity to meet students from different cities, cultures, and backgrounds. Sharing rooms, helping each other, solving daily problems together, and adapting to a new environment taught me valuable life lessons. These experiences made me more confident, patient, and mature as a person.
